newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark seen under 1.5175 after pause.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark seen under 1.5175 after pause.

text.p: Dollar/mark should consolidate in the near term, after its recent selloff achieved a key retracement objective, but will probably undergo another downswing before finding its legs, technicians said.

"I think we probably finish off 50-percent of the move of the whole summer rally, which would bring us down to 1.5050 marks," said Randolph Donney, director of capital markets at Pegasus Econometric Group.
Since hitting a four-and-a-half-month high at 1.5454 marks last week, the dollar has declined steadily, setting a new daily low of 1.5175 on Thursday.
The low to-date marks a 62-percent retracement of the rise from the September low at 1.50 marks to last week's high.
A slew of dollar/mark highs set in September before the last blast above 1.52 are located in the mid-1.51 region.
Dollar/mark may encounter strong support there and traders should be cautious shorting it below 1.51, analysts said.

"I don't think being real negative dollar/mark at this point (offers) good reward, given the risk," said Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc. "Sure you can get down to 1.50, but I think there is going to be a lot of interest at 1.5130 and 1.5100."

Meanwhile, after stalling just above 113 this week, dollar/yen is still seen shooting for the January 1994 high of 113.58, which Morden termed a "self-fulfilling objective". But the analysts said they would not be buying dollar/yen at these levels, noting that the last incremental highs were more a byproduct of yen weakness on crosses and the dollar move seemed to be losing steam.

"When the dollar starts to go down again versus the mark, and people start thinking they have bigger fish to fry, instead of trading the cross ... by that time I think you'll see a strong move out of dollar/yen," Donney said.
Morden said short positions should not be initiated unless the dollar breaks below 111.78 yen, saying in the medium term dollar/yen was probably still a buy.
At 1400 EDT on Thursday, dollar/yen was quoted at 112.81/84 compared to 112.72/77 at the U.S. open. Dollar/mark was at 1.5202/07,off from 1.5220/25.
